title: Density-Adaptive Bitmask Encoding: Fixed Chunks with Sparse Lexical Repair
description: Modern subword tokenizers allocate lexical capacity through a fixed segmentation policy rather than through local span difficulty. This paper studies Density-Adaptive Bitmask Encoding (DABE), a learned tokenizer-autoencoder that compresses fixed 64-token GPT-2-token chunks into binary codes and spends sparse lexical repair capacity only where reconstruction is difficult. Across controlled TinyStories experiments, fixed chunks plus adaptive sparse lexical repair outperform matched fixed-rate learned compression and variable-window alternatives at approximately 20 bits/token.
